newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rejects new ValuJet probe -- report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rejects new ValuJet probe -- report.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation has denied a union demand for an investigation into the government review of ValuJet Inc's bid to resume flight service, a newspaper reported on Friday.
The Atlanta Journal-Constitution quoted acting DOT Inspector General Joyce Fleischman as saying a probe was not warranted.
The Association of Flight Attendants has alleged that the government overlooked numerous issues when it gave the airline tentative approval on August 29 to resume flights.
DOT must issue final approval before ValuJet can schedule and book flights. An unnamed federal official was quoted by the newspaper as saying the final ruling may not come until next week.

ValuJet has been grounded since June 18, after a Federal Aviation Administration inspection that found numerous safety problems in the aftermath of the crash of ValuJet Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades on May 11, in which 110 people were killed.
